findings.problem: The architecture figure (five services, four databases, the data-access layer bar) is wrapped in a 96% scale (const SC = 0.96; V.place(fig, {s: SC})), so every label in it renders below the 28 px minimum: the 28 px card text comes out at 26.9 px. Affected text: Web app, Mobile API, Reports, Search, Billing (26.9 px for 5.8 s), Users DB, Orders DB, Products DB, Logs DB (26.9 px for 8.4 s) and data-access layer (26.9 to 27.3 px for 3.9 s). This is the figure the whole scene is about, and it is on screen from 3.6 s to the end.
findings.fix: Keep the wrapper but pre-compensate the font: right after D1.arch(fig, ...) set the text size on the arch cards to 28 / SC = 29.2 px, e.g. a.el.querySelectorAll(':scope > .v-card').forEach((c) => (c.style.fontSize = `${(28 / SC).toFixed(1)}px`)) (the helper never touches fontSize). Tried in the page at 29.2 px (effective 28.1 px): nothing wraps or overflows, but the two widest labels get tight ('Mobile API' fills 155 of 161 px and 'Products DB' 167 of 176 px of their cards), so check the frame after the change and, if it looks cramped, widen the cards by a few px in D1.arch. Better long term: give D1.arch an inset option (cards 12 px in from each side, no wrapper) so nothing needs scaling.
findings.evidence: Rendered-text scan of ds-1 at 0.1 s steps (effective px = computed font-size x cumulative transform scale): s10 local 3.6 to 11.9 s, scale 0.964 (layer bar 0.974). Stills ds-1-s10-4.2, s10-6, s10-8, s10-10.2 (absolute 105.7, 107.5, 109.5, 111.7 s).

findings.fix: Shorten and lengthen the windows a little: [0.75, 3.1] 'Easy to run, understand and change.' (35 ch, 14.9 cps); [3.95, 6.1] 'Every service uses every database.' (34 ch, 15.8); [6.3, 8.2] 'Swap a database: edit all five.' (31 ch, 16.3); [8.35, 10.4] 'A layer in between: 9 connections.' (34 ch, 16.6); [10.5, 12.1] 'Now only the layer changes.' (27 ch, 16.9). None of these start before their picture (badges land by 6.4 s, layer by 8.45 s, edit count by 10.4 s).

findings.problem: Caption 2, 'A cache keeps answers close: 2 ms, not 100.' (4.4 to 7.2 s), runs ahead of its picture. Until 5.35 s the cache panel shows only the first request and the red 'miss'; the '100 ms' tag arrives at 5.35 s, the purple copy only lands in the cache at about 5.85 s, and the '2 ms' tag at 6.35 s (hit tick 6.25 s). So for roughly the first 1 s the caption quotes a claim nothing on screen shows yet, and the number '2 ms, not 100' is on the caption about 2 s before either tag exists.
findings.fix: Make the caption start when the claim is visible: either retime the cache panel so '100 ms' lands by about 5.0 s and '2 ms' by about 5.8 s (start req2 and the hit about 0.5 s earlier), or start the caption at about 5.9 s with a shorter sentence ('A cache answers in 2 ms, not 100.', 33 characters, window 5.9 to 7.75 s = 17.8 cps) and let caption 3 start at 7.8 s as now.
findings.evidence: ds-1-s4-4.8 (30.3 s): caption fully shown, only 'miss' on screen. ds-1-s4-6.0 (31.5 s): '100 ms' visible, no '2 ms' yet. Timeline constants T.slow = 5.35, T.copy = [5.5, 5.85], T.fast = 6.35.

findings.problem: Most captions type their numbers by hand instead of taking them from the asserted helpers (house rule: never type a result by hand; scene 6 does it right with template strings). Hand-typed in strings: scene 4 '2 ms, not 100', '20 checks'; scene 5 '10,000 disks: about one dies...' plus the tags '10,000 disks' and '1 in 10,000 dies each day' (D1.DISKS.n and .p exist); scene 7 'The average is 250 ms', 'p95: 95 in 100', 'p99: 99 in 100'; scene 8 '3 lookups', '65 to 1', '345,000 a second', '87 seconds'; scene 9 '8 times', '£34,297 vs £8,800', '0% left, or 88% left', '40 times'; scene 10 '9 connections'. Every value is correct today, but none is asserted, so a change to the data (for example the fan-out figures another reviewer questions) would leave the caption silently wrong while the picture updates.
findings.fix: Build the caption strings from the data like scene 6 does: `The average is ${P.mean} ms.`, `Scale up costs more: ${D1.money(S.up8)} vs ${D1.money(S.out8)}.`, `${D1.fmt(T.load.writes2)} a second`, `${T.celeb.secs} seconds`, `${M.layered} connections`, D1.fmt(D1.DISKS.n) for '10,000', and so on, so the existing D1.same checks cover them.
